idea short_wide_block_width: focus shape [1,1,32,16384] R=1 C=512 pins bw=8/512B/64cores exactly at MIN_BLOCK_ROW_BYTES floor. Since R=1, num_blocks_total==num_w_chunks identically, so core count and read-transaction size are the SAME knob on this geometry -- doubling bw necessarily halves cores. Building bench in perf_experiments/short_wide_block_width using the existing lever-test monkeypatch trick (force _largest_divisor_at_most) to sweep bw in {2,4,8,16,32} plus ablation (reads/writes/compute) to separate read-stage, write-stage and whole-op wall.

assigned idea reader_bank_rotate: stagger reader stick-read issue ORDER per core so 64 cores spread across 12 DRAM banks instead of lockstep hammering bank r%12 at step r. Read reader kernel (tilize_reader.cpp reader_read_block branch) + helper (tilize_helpers_dataflow.inl read_sticks_for_tilize TILE mode) + host descriptor (reader_rt_args = [in_addr,start_block_id,num_blocks,block_stride], start_block_id==w_chunk on focus shape). Confirmed page->bank mapping is page_id % num_banks via tensor_accessor.h get_bank_and_offset_from_page_id. Plan: monkeypatch tilize_program_descriptor.KERNEL_DIR + _ablation_defines from my own test file (no edits to real op files) to point at perf_experiments/reader_bank_rotate/kernels/ with a modified reader that adds TILIZE_ROTATE_VARIANT/TILIZE_ROTATE_STRIDE compile defines, only touching the reader_read_block else-branch; writer/compute copied verbatim.

pytest collection error (RuntimeError: bernoulli already registered) when test file lived directly under perf_experiments/<slug>/ with no __init__.py: pytest importlib fallback module_name_from_path builds a rootdir-relative dotted name ttnn.ttnn.operations.tilize.perf_experiments...  which forces insert_missing_modules to import_module("ttnn.ttnn") as a SEPARATE namespace-resolved submodule, re-executing ttnn/ttnn/__init__.py a second time and double-registering C++ ops. Fixed by adding empty __init__.py to perf_experiments/ and perf_experiments/short_wide_block_width/ so the normal resolve_pkg_root_and_module_name path succeeds instead (module name resolves to plain ttnn.operations.tilize.perf_experiments... reusing cached sys.modules). All 5 forced bw variants (2,4,8,16,32) on focus shape now pass bit-identity.

idea short_wide_block_width VERDICT=NULL. Focus shape [1,1,32,16384] (R=1,C=512): forced bw in {2,4,8,16,32} via _largest_divisor_at_most monkeypatch, 3 fresh-cache profiled runs each, all bit-identity PASS. Medians: bw2=15534(+13.7%) bw4=13319(-2.5%, flips sign run-to-run = flat/null) bw8=13664(baseline/production) bw16=14293(+4.6%, consistent regression all 3 runs paired) bw32=16077(+17.7%, consistent regression). Read/write stage split (TILIZE_ABLATE) at bw16 shows READ stage alone IS faster (6635 vs 7675ns, -14%) but occupancy loss (32 vs 64 cores) still costs more in the full op -- confirms bank-spread/parallelism dominates transaction size here, not the reverse. Structural finding: since tensor_row_blocks=R=1, num_blocks_total==num_w_chunks identically -- there is NO way to reach a >=1024B read without giving up cores on this geometry; derive_plan already never attempts it (occupancy target dominates the max() at waves=1 before the floor is even consulted). Confirmed same pattern on short_wide_wide [1,1,32,32768] (also R=1, production bw=8/64cores/512B): forced bw16 (32 cores/1024B) regressed +4.6% and +6.1% across 2 reps. Verdict: current derive_plan solve is already optimal on R=1 geometries; no rule change recommended. Artifact: ttnn/ttnn/operations/tilize/perf_experiments/short_wide_block_width/test_short_wide_block_width.py. Also fixed a pytest collection bug (empty __init__.py needed under perf_experiments/ and the slug dir) that would otherwise break any sibling test file placed directly under perf_experiments/<slug>/.

coord_reuse_raw and combined variants HUNG the device (NocHangError, required auto-reset): raw NOC_CMD_BUF_WRITE_REG(NOC_RET_ADDR_COORDINATE) with no noc_cmd_buf_ready guard races the hardware draining the prior in-flight write. Fixed by adding while(!noc_cmd_buf_ready(noc_index,write_cmd_buf)); before the raw coordinate write, matching what ncrisc_noc_write_set_state/_with_state already do internally. Also discovered TensorAccessor for a plain interleaved DRAM tensor resolves via partial specialization to an InterleavedAddrGen-based type (tensor_accessor.h:379-394), NOT the generic get_bank_and_offset/dspec() API -- rewrote addr-recurrence variants to use interleaved_addr_gen::get_bank_offset_index/get_bank_index/get_noc_xy directly. Also discovered baseline divide is already a compile-time-constant-divisor magic-multiply (udivsi3_const_divisor), not a naive runtime division -- addr-recurrence savings are smaller than assumed.

All 22 non-profiled correctness dispatches PASS (baseline/addr_recurrence/coord_reuse_raw/combined x 5 shapes + 2 fabric-backpressure probes); set_state_naive XFAILs on focus shape as predicted (bit-mismatch, wrong DRAM bank). Proceeding to --profile run for device ns numbers.

writer_dual_risc: REGRESSION on every tested regime. decisive check showed store is bandwidth-bound not issue-bound at 64 cores (writer_issue 643ns@4cores -> 4154ns@64cores, not flat). col_split (candidate A) measured 1.5-1.7x worse (focus 13142->19962ns); role_swap (candidate C) measured 1.5-2.5x worse (focus 13142->33340ns), matching the predicted NoC read/write directional asymmetry. Both built and measured; option B not built (would only add semaphore overhead on top of the same losing mechanism). Correctness: all variants bit-identical where expressible; col_split inexpressible at block_width_tiles=1 (tall_narrow, small).

writer_issue zone (ns) run1: baseline focus=3204 addr_recurrence=3344(+4.4%) coord_reuse_raw=3522(+9.9%) combined=3370(+5.2%) naive=13409(4.2x WORSE, and incorrect). Decisive fabric test: full-grid(64 cores)=4337ns/8writes=542ns/call vs single-core=545ns/8writes=68ns/call -- 8x collapse => confirms fabric back-pressure dominates, not RISC issue cost. All state-reuse variants flat-to-regression, never a win. Rerunning focus shape 2 more times for noise-band confirmation before finalizing verdict as NULL/mild-regression.

writer_bank_rotate: NULL on focus shape [1,1,32,16384] (baseline median 13542ns vs rotate_chunk median 13246ns, -2.2%, within +-8% noise band). Modest mean-only WIN at square_mid [1,1,1024,1024] (baseline median 24404ns vs rotate_chunk median 22767ns, -6.7%, consistent x3 repeats) but tail (max/mean BRISC span) got slightly WORSE there (1.24x->1.29x), so it is not a tail-flattening win. short_wide_wide [1,1,32,32768] leaned +3.7% slower (within noise, 3 repeats same direction - flagged not confirmed). tall_narrow/small are bw=1 so column rotation is a no-op; only rotate_rows_cols (mode 4) moved tall_narrow (-3.6%, single run). All 5 modes x 5 shapes passed bit-identity (25/25). Zone report shows writer_wait_out (starvation on upstream reader/compute) is 61-72% of BRISC kernel span across all shapes, capping how much an issue-order-only lever can move the needle. Flagged host-side block_id->core permutation (menu item 6) as a more promising unexplored lever for the coordinator since a blocks own bank-SET is fixed regardless of issue order.

NULL at whole-op DEVICE KERNEL DURATION level for all 4 correct variants across all 5 shapes (all within +-8% noise band, several reruns taken). At the writer_issue zone level: addr_recurrence flat-to-mildly-worse everywhere (division was already a compile-time-const-divisor magic-multiply, not naive division, so nothing to save); coord_reuse_raw reproducibly WORSE on wide_short (+16-24% across 2 runs) and tall_narrow (noisy, small absolute ns); combined inherits both, net flat-to-worse. set_state_naive is INCORRECT (xfail, wrong DRAM bank) AND ~4.2x slower (bank-hotspot convergence). Decisive fabric-vs-RISC test: focus-shape per-core geometry (8 writes) at 64-cores-active = 542 ns/write vs 1-core-active = 68 ns/write -- 8x collapse proves the ~540ns/call issue cost the coordinator measured is NoC/DRAM fabric back-pressure from 64 cores sharing 12 banks, not RISC-side command-programming cost. That is the root cause every state-reuse variant is a null/regression: the lever only touches the ~68ns uncontended RISC slice (13% of the total), and the correctness-required noc_cmd_buf_ready guard my raw-LLK variant needed ate even that. Writing final report now.

reader_bank_rotate = WIN on the reader stage in isolation (reads-only ablation TILIZE_ABLATE=writes,compute, 2 reps median): focus shape attention NCRISC mean 5545->4769ns (-14.0%) max 7139->6178ns (-13.5%); short_wide_wide -6.7%/-4.9%; width_chunked -7.7%/-8.9%; square_mid FLAT (+0.8%/-2.3%, partial lockstep); tall_narrow FLAT (-2.2%/-2.2%, disjoint per-core ranges, matches mechanism prediction of no lockstep to fix). raw-loop-vs-helper control (variant1, r0=0) gave ~0-2% alone, confirming the rotation itself (not bypassing the helper) is the mechanism. All rotation strides {1,5,7,11,13} and the bank-exact formula (variant3) win by statistically the same ~13-18%, no ordering by stride -- recommend stride=1 (reuses w_chunk directly, zero extra derivation, cheapest). Spread (max/mean NCRISC) stays ~1.03-1.3x across baseline AND rotated variants per shape -- rotation moves mean+tail down PROPORTIONALLY, does not disproportionately flatten the tail. Whole-op DEVICE KERNEL DURATION barely moves (attention -2.1%, others within +-3%) because BRISC(writer) KERNEL span stays flat (~9900-10100ns) regardless of reader variant -- writer dominates wall on this op structure (matches shared context: writes 55% share vs reads 33%), so the reader win is real but currently hidden by the writer bottleneck; flagging for coordinator that writer_bank_rotate/other writer-side wins would be needed to surface this in the whole-op number. Bit-identity (torch.equal) verified for every variant on all 5 shapes in un-ablated runs. Reporting final result now.
